### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **87** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/security-catalog-namespace.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**53** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2f80f2897a4c484c9ff445d268ab83e1ce16a6d0`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/security-catalog-namespace.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **62** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2f80f2897a4c484c9ff445d268ab83e1ce16a6d0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6a5b6a286cb4a7bdb3511d750086dbbc6578911f` — the merge of head `a79fe6e12ea8157d2a722505ca81e19ef1ef5a09` into base `2f80f2897a4c484c9ff445d268ab83e1ce16a6d0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6a5b6a286cb4a7bdb3511d750086dbbc6578911f && git checkout 6a5b6a286cb4a7bdb3511d750086dbbc6578911f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2f80f2897a4c484c9ff445d268ab83e1ce16a6d0 a79fe6e12ea8157d2a722505ca81e19ef1ef5a09 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2f80f2897a4c484c9ff445d268ab83e1ce16a6d0 && git merge --no-ff a79fe6e12ea8157d2a722505ca81e19ef1ef5a09

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2f80f2897a4c484c9ff445d268ab83e1ce16a6d0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2f80f2897a4c484c9ff445d268ab83e1ce16a6d0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review + epic red-line read · 2026-11-12T14:51Z

Head-sha: `37f7bcf6abb03a187df895a4c4e5ea74ed976f16` (merge base with main: cac0f1aab). Scope: all non-test source in the diff, plus the pins. Reviewed-by: session_01L6bhgXQnNkXTT1Wu7i7Y3i.
Verdict: **PASS-with-nits.** No must-fix.

**Epic red lines**
1. Resolution never loosened: PASS. Admission happens only where two addresses exist; the stored-column rule only tightens.
2. Ambiguity reported, never guessed: PASS. Two metadata slots or two holders give a refusal naming both (`security-catalog.ts` ~764-783). Lock, echo and ledger act per holder.
3. Independently releasable: PASS. Additive. Positions, capabilities, the environment and built-ins keep one holder; declared.

**Declarations.** Clause-② yes (widening) matches in body and changeset. FROM→TO tables match the code: the install door, item seam and save door admit; `sys` / `base` / `guest_portal` / no-namespace / co-owner rows stay refused. One predicate: `permissionSetHoldersMeet` (`packages/core/src/permission-set-holders.ts:52`) has three callers, the registry (package door and item seam via `securityCatalogHoldersOtherThan`) and the save door. Nothing else spells it. Ruling A (6824698376) holds on this head: `servable()` gates both the registry item and the new metadata-slot read, so a disabled holder's bound grant confers nothing and is not re-targeted (row-9 pins :353-420). Every stored-column reader goes through `storedPermissionSetScope` into the one catalog arm; no bypass reader found; it fails closed when the column's package is missing or has no namespace.

**Merge hazard with #32497.** It is in the stored-column arm of `resolvePermissionScoped` (`security-catalog.ts` ~682-721). Whichever PR lands second keeps the disabled-holder check ahead of the slot read and re-takes the row-9 pins.

**Before landing (text and declarations only, rides the main-merge push, no code round)**
1. The save door's 422 sentence tail changes (`protocol-save-door-refusals.ts` ~467-472: "one name per deployment … See ADR-0048" becomes "one name per namespace … See ADR-0150 D2"). The envelope (`NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`, 422) does not change. Add a FROM→TO row and drop "unchanged in envelope and sentence" from the body and changeset.
2. `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` names its card: #32758 (spec describe `permission.zod.ts:1207-1208` and `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx:430`).
3. Changeset levels: `@objectstack/metadata` and `@objectstack/plugin-security` are moved by the diff but take `patch`. Under AGENTS.md Post-Task 3, a `Metadata-protocol: added` kind takes at least `minor` on a moved package. Raise them, or cite the changeset gate's verdict.
4. The body states that "Narrowing: no" covers the name rule, and that the stored-column rule is the declared hardening (the moved pins in five files carry FROM→TO).

**Nits → follow-up #32753 (parked per 6824949405)**
- `protocol-permission-set-name-registry-reading.test.ts:326` pins `PERMISSION_SET_SHARED_NAMESPACES` against `[...RESERVED_NAMESPACES, 'sys']` and not against the registry's `isShareableNamespace`, so a change to that function alone would not go red.
- `catalog-reference-report.ts` ~366: a stale column refused as ambiguous lands in the generic "does not resolve" bucket instead of the "outside namespace" line. It confers nothing either way.
- `security-catalog-echo.ts:317`: the tenant-authored check asks the lock by bare name. With two holders, an environment-authored set bound to another namespace's package may classify as packaged. This is not verified; it needs a pin.

**Measured at head (dependency closure built):** objectql registry-reading 17/17; core `security-catalog` + `grant-set-by-name` 67/67; metadata cluster 61/61; plugin-security, 8 files, 171/171.
**Ablations (each reverted):** A, the predicate without the shared-namespace and `guest_portal` lines: 8 of 17 red. B, the save door with a plain namespace compare: 6 of 17 red. C, the item seam given no namespace: 2 red. D, the namespace check removed from the stored-column arm: core 2 of 67 and plugin-security 5 of 106 red.
Not checked: CI runs (the gate is on the landing head).

## Contract review delta (merge-forward) + epic red-line read · 2026-11-12T15:06Z

Head-sha: `3f931144b13df25d26b1f28ba13549d281f66358`. Since the reviewed head (record 6826951220) there are two commits: a merge of main f7a0fe0ea, and one commit that touches only the changeset. Size: 36 files, +2434 −315 (2749 lines). Reviewed-by: session_01L6bhgXQnNkXTT1Wu7i7Y3i.
Verdict: **PASS.**

Merge-forward test (the PR's diff against its old merge base, compared with its diff against main): the only code that differs is the #32739 conflict. Main now owns `mutationEventPackage(packageId)` in `protocol-mutation-package.ts`, so the PR's type-gated helper is renamed `projectorEventPackage(type, packageId)` and returns `mutationEventPackage(packageId)` for `permission` (with a stated binding) and `{}` otherwise. The six call sites (item save, commit, restore, rollback, the permission landing door, layered) are renamed one for one. The one change in meaning: the projector event's `packageId` now passes through main's `boundPackageOf`, so an empty id or the package-less `'sys_metadata'` sentinel reads as `null` (no package), where the old helper passed the value through. That agrees with how the catalog echo reads a package-less row and confers nothing more. The red lines are unchanged.

The four should-fix items from 6826951220 are discharged in the changeset and body: the save door's 422 sentence has its FROM → TO row, and "unchanged sentence" now reads "same envelope"; `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — #32758`; `@objectstack/metadata` and `@objectstack/plugin-security` are `minor` (Post-Task 3); and the body says "Narrowing: no" covers the name rule, with the stored-column rule as the declared hardening.
Measured by the card thread at this head: closure build and type-check of the 5 packages exit 0; metadata-protocol 22786, metadata 1884, core 3353, plugin-security 6524 (45 skipped), objectql 22/22. CI is the landing gate.

> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）

- **Merge-forward read: PASS.** Parents are the last read head a75461f30 and main 2f80f2897, which carries #32497 (0763bf6ec). The remerge diff has one conflicted file, `packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts`, with two hunks; nothing else moved beyond main's own changes.
